**New move button:**
- Add a new "move" button (e.g. a ↔ or ⇔ icon) to the right of the existing left/right arrow buttons in the chord editing popover.
- Clicking this button enters "move mode" for that chord.
- While in move mode, replace the move button with a "commit" button (✓ or "v") that, when clicked, exits move mode and keeps the chord at its current position.

**Move mode behaviour:**
- Remove all `mousedown`-based drag logic. The chord should not be dragged; instead it passively follows the horizontal mouse cursor position (`mousemove` on the document or a suitable container) while move mode is active.
- Map the mouse's X position within the line's rendered text area to a `charIndex` value, updating the chord's position in `pendingChords` in real time as the mouse moves.
- Pressing Escape or clicking outside should cancel move mode and revert the chord to its position before move mode was entered (consistent with existing ✕ / click-outside behaviour).

**Boundary constraint logic:**
- While moving a chord, clamp its `charIndex` so that it stays strictly between the positions of its neighbours:
 - **Lower bound:** `charIndex` of the previous chord in the line + 1, or `0` if there is no previous chord.
 - **Upper bound:** `charIndex` of the next chord in the line - 1, or `line.text.length - 1` if there is no next chord.
- The chord must never be allowed to land on or past an adjacent chord's `charIndex`, preventing swapping or overwriting of neighbours (unlike the current arrow-button swap behaviour, move mode is
